title: Customer network incident runbook using approval logs (wip)
content:
Purpose:
This runbook describes how to investigate, contain, and remediate customer-managed network incidents by correlating operator approval gates, immutable approval receipts, and network telemetry. Goal is to give SREs, customer-facing ops, and PMs a repeatable checklist for producing a verifiable evidence package for customers and auditors.

Scope:
- Applies to Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) where changes to customer-managed network components are gated by Redwood approval flow (operator approvals, delegated admin assertions).
- Focus on incidents triggered by unauthorized changes, mis-routed peering, accidental firewall rule deletions, and unexpected route announcements.
- Excludes infra-side hardware failures not caused by network config changes.

Assumptions / prerequisites:
- Approval receipts are captured and stored in the immutable approval ledger (sha256-signed receipts + timestamp).
- Audit logs (control plane + operator actions) are exported to customer-observed bucket and to Redwood S3 retention for 90 days by default (configurable per-customer).
- Network telemetry (BGP sessions, peering health, route tables, firewall logs) is available for the impacted perimeter.
- On-call SRE and customer success lead contactable.

Quick triage checklist (first 15 minutes):
1) Confirm customer report and gather initial scope (affected services, TL;DR symptoms). Note time of detection.
2) Pull approval ledger entries for the 60 minutes prior to symptom time: approval-ids, approver, rationale field, and cryptographic receipt.
   - Command (internal): /opt/infra/bin/approval-fetch --customer {CID} --since "-60m" --json > approvals.json
3) Check control plane audit log for matching change IDs and operator IDs.
   - Look for: change_id == approval.change_id, operator_email, ip origin, session id.
4) Retrieve network telemetry snapshots (route table, firewall rules, peering status) at T-5 and T+5 around the change if available.

Containment play (if change appears malicious or accidental but still live):
- If change is isolated to a specific VPC or peering connection, trigger the isolation workflow: revoke ephemeral access, disable the specific route advertisement, and lock operator account (soft lock) while preserving audit trail.
  - Steps:
    a) Issue API call to pause customer-managed route propagation: /api/v1/private/vpcs/{vpc}/propagation?state=paused
    b) Create an immutable evidence snapshot (see Evidence package section).
    c) Notify CS and customer liaison.
- If change impacts control plane reachability broadly, escalate to SEV and follow full incident coordination.

Evidence package (what to include for customer & audit):
- Immutable approval receipts (raw receipts + human-readable extracted fields).
- Control plane audit log slices (ISO timestamps, change ids, operator id).
- Network telemetry snapshots (route tables, firewall configuration, BGP announcements) with timestamps and hashes.
- Replayable sequence of API calls that reproduce the change (redact any secrets).
- Snapshot of RBAC/entitlements for approver accounts at the time of change.
- Incident timeline (human summary) with links to above artifacts.
- Minimal integrity manifest: a small JSON file listing artifact filenames + SHA256 checksums + signer info.

Forensics tips / sample artifacts format:
- Approval receipt example (trimmed):
  {
    "approval_id": "apr_0a9f...",
    "approver": "ops+alice@customer.com",
    "change_id": "chg_47b2...",
    "time": "2025-02-12T18:23:44Z",
    "signature": "MEUCIQD...",
    "rationale": "upgrade route filter for peering"
  }
- Control plane log entry (text):
  2025-02-12T18:23:45Z | change_id=chg_47b2 | operator=ops+alice@customer.com | action=update_route_table | target=vpc-42 | diff=+10.0.0.0/8 -> withdraw
- Network snapshot naming convention: cust-{CID}-snapshot-{YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ}.tar.gz

Rollback guidance:
- Preferred: automated rollback using recorded previous config state. If previous state unknown: consult last successful snapshot and reapply.
- Commands (examples):
  - rollback route table: /privatectl --cid {CID} --vpc {vpc} rollback-route --change-id {change_id}
  - if privatectl unavailable, apply manual rule set from snapshot: /privatectl apply-config --file snapshot.json

Escalation matrix:
- P0 (major outage): Page SRE lead + Head of Product + Customer Success lead immediately. Open SEV channel.
- P1 (degraded but contained): Page on-call SRE + responsible SE.
- Provide the evidence package link and approval receipts in the first 30 minutes.

Post-incident controls & follow-up:
- 1:1 with approver(s) to validate intent. Capture learnings and update the approval rationale taxonomy if free-text entries are ambiguous.
- If approval process bypassed or signs of compromise found, rotate operator keys and require re-attestation of delegated admin principals.
- Propose product changes (shortlist):
   * enforce 'intent templates' for approval forms (structured fields),
   * require step-up 2FA for network-impacting approvals,
   * automated pre-change simulation that warns on high-risk diffs.

Retention & compliance notes:
- Default retention for approval receipts: 365 days. Control plane audit logs: 90 days (configurable). Telemetry: 30 days.
- For customers requesting longer retention (audit/regulatory), raise contract amendment (linked_artifacts: JIRA-NET-1347).

Automation ideas (short experiments):
- Auto-generate evidence package after every approval that touches routing/firewall objects. Keep ephemeral snapshot for 7 days and store long-term on-demand when change is promoted.
- Implement a 'safety-score' that runs a dry-run against the customer's current traffic model and flags approvals exceeding a threshold.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Who owns the legal copy of the immutable ledger for on-prem customers? (ops vs customer)
- Define schema for the integrity manifest (small JSON with checksums + signer IDs) and bake into approval pipeline.
- Decide on default retention windows per compliance tier and reflect in billing.

Notes to self / meeting anchors:
- Demo this runbook with SRE + CS in March weekly ops review.
- Sync with Security team on allowed remediation actions (account locks, forced rollback vs soft rollback).

References and links:
- ephemeral scripts repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy-scripts (PR#58)
- Related confluence draft: confluence://private-deployments/approval-evidence-spec (work in progress)

Contact list (who to page):
- On-call SRE: pagers on rotation (see internal rota)
- CS escalation: cs-esc@redwood.com
- Security incident lead: sec-incident@redwood.com

Changelog (short):
- 2025-02-14: initial draft, basic flow and evidence checklist (Ava)
- 2025-02-21: added automation ideas and P0/P1 escalation matrix (Ravi)
- 2025-03-02: clarified retention defaults and example artifacts (Leah)

END OF DRAFT

(Work-in-progress: tidy prose later, convert some steps into executable runbook cards for PagerDuty integration.)
